create.subtitleMcp: One key per assistant or workstation, so you can revoke each on its own

created.title: Key “{name}” created.

revoke.title: Revoke “{name}”?
revoke.impactClientsValue: Scripts and services with this key are rejected.
revoke.impactClientsMcp: Assistants with this key lose access.
revoke.impactReversibleValue: No, you will need a new key.

explainer.title: What are API keys for?
explainer.what: A key replaces the sign-in when a program rather than a person talks to LCM.
explainer.read: Queries yes, changes no. Good for monitoring and reports.
explainer.readwrite: May do everything you may, including changing servers and starting jobs.
explainer.rights: A key always acts with the rights of the account that created it. If that account changes its password, its keys become invalid.
explainer.header: The program sends the key in the header of every request:

schedule.title: Automatic backup
schedule.subtitle: LCM backs up the database, master key and configuration on a schedule.
schedule.blocked: The automatic backup cannot run: it is encrypted, and an unattended backup needs recipient keys or a passphrase. Set one of them below.
schedule.enableOn: LCM backs up on the schedule below. An overdue backup is made up shortly after start.
schedule.enableOff: Only backups you trigger by hand exist.
schedule.intervalHint: If the interval divides the day (6, 12, 24), backups run at fixed times.
schedule.timeHint: Anchor of the schedule in server time.

keys.title: Encryption
keys.subtitle: Every backup is encrypted. Without the matching key it cannot be opened.
keys.recipientsHint: Public keys (age1…). If set, LCM encrypts to them instead of using the passphrase. To open a backup you need a private key that never lives on the server.
keys.generateHelp: Creates a new key pair. The public key goes into the list, the private key is shown exactly once.
keys.generateMeaning: Store the private key safely before you leave the page. The public key applies only after "Save".
keys.generatedText: It appears only this once and exists nowhere else. Without it no backup encrypted to it can be opened.
keys.passphraseHint: Applies only without recipient keys. Leave empty to keep the stored passphrase.
keys.autoRestartOn: LCM restarts itself after a restore and applies it. This needs systemd or Docker.
keys.autoRestartOff: The restore stays prepared and applies at the next start.

list.title: Created backups
list.subtitle: Download, restore or delete.
list.empty: No backups yet. "Back up now" creates the first one.

create.label: Back up now
create.help: Immediately creates an encrypted backup of the database, master key and configuration.
create.meaning: You then have a state you can return to.
create.title: Create backup now
create.message: LCM backs up the current state.

encryption.missing: None stored, enter a passphrase below

restore.label: Restore
restore.title: Restore and reset LCM?
restore.message: LCM resets itself to the state of {name}.
restore.expect: Type the file name to confirm: {name}
restore.impactSessionsValue: All end, you must sign in again
restore.impactReversibleValue: No. Create a backup of the current state first.
restore.restartManual: You have to restart LCM yourself afterwards

delete.label: Delete {name}
delete.title: Delete backup?
delete.impactRestoreValue: This state can no longer be restored afterwards

upload.title: Restore from file
upload.subtitle: Upload a downloaded backup, for example when moving to a new installation.

staged.title: Restore prepared.
staged.auto: LCM restarts in a moment and signs you out. Sign in again in a few seconds.
staged.manual: Restart LCM for it to apply.

explainer.title: How does LCM back up?
explainer.what: A backup contains the database, the master key and the configuration. It is always encrypted.
explainer.recipients: LCM only knows the public part. No secret lives on the server.
explainer.passphrase: LCM stores it encrypted so scheduled backups can run.
explainer.restore: A restore replaces everything with the state of the backup. It applies after the restart.

servers.title: Default name servers
servers.subtitle: This list is offered when you set the DNS entries of a server.
servers.label: Name servers
servers.hint: One per line as "name = IP" or just the IP. Empty uses the built-in list.

domains.title: Test domains
domains.subtitle: The DNS test checks on the server whether these domains resolve.
domains.label: Domains
domains.hint: One domain per line. Empty uses the built-in list.

form.leaveText: This page has unsaved changes. They will be lost if you leave.
form.loadFailed: The settings could not be loaded
form.discardMessage: What you entered here will be lost.

ssh.title: Defaults for new servers
ssh.subtitle: User and port LCM pre-fills for new servers.

key.title: Onboarding key
key.subtitle: LCM created it on first start. The private part stays encrypted inside LCM.
key.how: Add the public key to ~/.ssh/authorized_keys of root on the new server. Then add or reconnect the server with "system SSH key", no password needed.
key.none: There is no key yet. LCM creates it on the next start.

address.title: Public address
address.subtitle: LCM builds the links in emails from it.
address.label: Address of this installation
address.hint: Scheme, host and port only, no path.
address.warning: Not set: links in emails come from the local configuration and may not be reachable from outside. LCM deliberately does not derive the address from the request, otherwise a password reset link could be steered to a foreign domain.

jobs.title: Monitoring
jobs.subtitle: When LCM treats a run as stuck and the packages of a server as outdated.
jobs.idleHint: If there is no output for this long, LCM aborts the run and frees the server. 0 turns the monitoring off.
jobs.idleSlowHint: For Raspberry Pi and servers with at most 2 cores and 2 GB RAM, where long silent phases are normal.
jobs.staleHint: How old the last successful package update may be before the server gets a warning.
jobs.staleCritHint: After that, LCM counts as unable to act on this server.

mail.title: Email sending
mail.subtitle: Outbox for password resets, invitations and notes to the admins.
mail.enableOn: LCM sends mail through the SMTP server below.
mail.enableOff: No mail leaves LCM. Password reset and invitations by email are unavailable.
mail.adminsHint: Separate several addresses with a comma.
mail.channelHint: Alert rules can then pick "Standard email (system)".
mail.channelOn: Alert rules can send mail to the admin recipients.
mail.channelOff: The channel is missing from the choices of alert rules.
mail.testHelp: Sends a test mail to the admin recipients so you can see whether sending works.
mail.testMeaning: The saved state is tested, not your unsaved changes.
mail.testSent: Test message sent. Check the inbox of the admin recipients.

keep.title: Retention
keep.subtitle: What LCM deletes after how long. Cleanup runs daily.
keep.logsHint: After this, LCM deletes job history and console output.
keep.routineHint: Health checks and alert evaluations run every few minutes. Their output disappears after this period; that the run happened stays visible until the general retention ends.
keep.storageHint: Daily values of disk usage. Allowed: 90 to 365 days.

session.title: Sign-in in the browser
session.subtitle: Where LCM keeps the browser sign-in and how long it lasts. Scripts and automation use an API key and are not affected.

memory.title: In memory only (safest option, default)
memory.text: The sign-in applies to this one tab only and lives in memory only. After a reload, in a new tab or after closing it you are signed out and sign in again. No cookie is set, nothing is written to disk.

cookie.title: Session cookie (more convenient, HTTPS only)
cookie.text: The sign-in applies to all tabs of this browser and survives a reload until you sign out or the session expires. The cookie is only sent over HTTPS and cannot be read by scripts; the content security policy (CSP) keeps foreign scripts from running. It stays in the browser for the duration of the session.

session.needsHttps: Only available when LCM is opened over HTTPS.

ask.title: How should sign-in work in the browser?
ask.lead: You decide this once for this installation and can change it later under Settings → General.

mailSecurity.label: Encryption
mailSecurity.noneWarning: The password and the content cross the network in plain text. Only use this in trusted networks.

mcp.hostLocal: Only a local address: 127.0.0.1, ::1 or localhost.

interface.title: Interface
interface.subtitle: AI assistants read the state of your fleet via MCP
interface.enableOn: LCM accepts MCP requests at the address below. An assistant needs an MCP key for that.
interface.enableOff: No MCP access. Existing MCP keys stay but have no effect.
interface.hostHint: MCP speaks unencrypted HTTP. For access from outside, put a TLS proxy or tunnel in front.

example.title: Connecting
example.subtitle: How to add LCM to an MCP client, using the saved address

explainer.title: What is MCP?
explainer.what: The Model Context Protocol connects AI assistants to tools. Through the interface an assistant asks, for example, which servers need updates or a reboot. It cannot change anything there.
explainer.local: The interface only listens locally, because keys and fleet data would otherwise travel the network in plain text.
explainer.keys: MCP keys only work here and act with the rights of the account that created them.

login.title: Sign-in
login.subtitle: Who needs a second factor
login.twofaRolesHint: Roles, comma separated. Anyone with one of them sets up 2FA at the next sign-in.
login.adminWarning: Administrators do not have to use a second factor. Whoever captures an admin password controls the SSH access of the whole fleet.
login.selfWarning: This includes you: after saving you must set up 2FA first before you can continue. Have your phone with an authenticator app ready.

session.ttlHint: 0 uses the default from the configuration file, otherwise 5 to 43200 (30 days).
session.ttlTooShort: At least 5 minutes, or 0 for the default.

cve.title: CVE scan
cve.subtitle: Daily check of installed packages against the vulnerability database (Trivy)
cve.enableOn: LCM checks the packages of all servers on schedule and reports known vulnerabilities.
cve.enableOff: No scan; the vulnerabilities found are no longer refreshed.
cve.cronHint: Minute hour day month weekday. Not 4 am, the system sync already runs then.
cve.cronInvalid: Not a valid cron expression: five fields or a shortcut like @daily.
cve.phasedOn: Updates that Ubuntu offers only to some systems count as available right away.
cve.phasedOff: Phased updates only count once Ubuntu releases them to the server.
cve.weightHint: Comma separated; their vulnerabilities count one level more severe. Empty uses the built-in list, a single - turns it off. postgresql also matches postgresql-14.

advisory.title: Early warning
advisory.subtitle: New advisories from OSV every 15 minutes, long before the next CVE scan finds them
advisory.privacy: For the online query your package inventory (names and versions, without server names) goes to the OSV service. With a local copy it stays in-house.
advisory.enableOn: LCM regularly asks OSV for advisories about your packages.
advisory.enableOff: New vulnerabilities only show up with the next CVE scan.
advisory.local: Local copy instead of online query
advisory.localOn: LCM mirrors the OSV data and checks against the copy. Advisories then arrive about a day later.
advisory.localOff: LCM asks OSV directly; the package inventory leaves the house for that.
advisory.ttlHint: 0 turns it off, at most 30. While a result is valid, LCM does not ask again for that package.
advisory.noSystems: None. Only once a server has reported its packages is there anything to mirror.
advisory.mirrorHelp: Downloads the OSV data of the mirrored systems again. That is a few megabytes and takes a few minutes.
advisory.mirrorMeaning: New advisories are in the early warning right afterwards.
advisory.mirrorFailed: The copy could not be updated. See the job for details.

activate.title: Activate subscription
activate.subtitle: The subscription brings support and the enterprise package channel. Community and enterprise are functionally the same, with no server limit.
activate.urlHint: Empty uses repo.techeve.de. Change it only if you run your own repository server.

subscription.activated: Subscription activated. The repository access is set up.
subscription.quota: Quota exceeded: you manage {managed} servers, the contract includes {included}. LCM restricts nothing.

verify.label: Check now
verify.help: Asks the subscription service for the current contract status.
verify.meaning: The status above is refreshed. Nothing changes in the contract.

subscription.verifyFailed: The contract status could not be checked

remove.label: Remove subscription
remove.title: Remove subscription?
remove.message: The subscription is deleted from this installation.
remove.impactAccessValue: Access to the enterprise package channel ends
remove.impactBindingValue: Stays until the provider releases it

apt.title: Package channel of the LCM host
apt.subtitle: Which channel LCM gets its own updates from.

community.label: Community channel
community.hint: Every stable release, right after publication.

beta.label: Beta channel
beta.hint: Pre-releases for testing, not for production. Final releases and security updates keep arriving.

enterprise.label: Enterprise channel
enterprise.hint: Vetted, approved releases. Security updates still arrive immediately.

apt.needsActive: The enterprise channel works only once the subscription is active.
apt.needsContract: The enterprise channel needs a subscription. Community and beta are free.
apt.applyHelp: Writes the package source of the chosen channel to the LCM host and removes the sources of the other channels.
apt.reapplyHelp: Rewrites the package source of the active channel, for enterprise also the credentials. Needed for hosts switched before this version.
apt.meaning: The next LCM updates come from this channel. The process runs as a job.
apt.unavailable: Not available: the LCM host is not registered as an apt server. Check the self-registration.

confirm.community: Updates then arrive immediately with every release again.
confirm.beta: The host then receives LCM pre-releases. This is meant for testing.
confirm.enterprise: The host then receives approved releases only.

apt.impactTargetValue: The LCM host (package source is rewritten)
apt.impactReversibleValue: Yes, you can switch back at any time
apt.failedHint: Details are in the job log.

instance.title: Instance ID
instance.subtitle: The permanent ID of this installation. It goes to the provider on activation and travels with the backup.

servers.title: Default time servers
servers.subtitle: This list is offered when you set up NTP on a server.
servers.label: Time servers
servers.hint: One per line as "name = host". Empty uses the built-in list (NTP pool, Cloudflare, Google).

zone.title: Default time zone
zone.subtitle: Pre-fills the "set time zone" form. You always set the time deliberately per server.
zone.label: Time zone
zone.hint: IANA format, for example Europe/Berlin. Empty gives no default.

list.subtitle: Who may sign in to LCM and with which rights

users.createSubtitle: The account can sign in with this password right away. To let it set its own password, send an activation link afterwards.

form.usernameHint: 3 to 32 characters: a–z, 0–9, _ and -. Cannot be changed later.
form.emailHint: Used for invitations and password resets.
form.emailInvalid: This is not a valid email address.
form.currentHint: Required because you are changing your own email address.
form.passwordHint: At least 12 characters; must not contain the name or email.
form.passwordRules: The password does not meet the rules yet.

menu.inviteHint: The account sets its own password; with an email address the link is mailed.
menu.passwordHint: All sessions end; a new password is due at the next sign-in.
menu.blockHint: No more sign-ins; the account is kept.

link.message: With this link the account sets its own password. It is valid until {until} and works only once.
link.mailed: The link is on its way to {email}.
link.mailFailed: The email could not be sent ({reason}). Pass the link on yourself.
link.noMail: The account has no email address. Pass the link on yourself.

password.title: Set password for {name}
password.message: Pass the new password on securely.
password.impactSessionsValue: All sessions and API keys of the account become invalid.
password.impactNextValue: The account must change the password immediately.

block.title: Block {name}?
block.message: The account is kept with its roles and settings.

unblock.title: Unblock {name}?
unblock.message: The account can then sign in again with its previous password.

delete.title: Delete {name}?
delete.message: If you only want to end the access, block the account instead.

discard.title: Discard changes?
discard.message: You have not saved here yet. If you close, the changes are lost.

action.meaning: What does it mean for you?

monitor.title: Monitoring
monitor.activeHint: An alert rule watches this and notifies through its channel.
monitor.logOnlyHint: The rule is active but has no channel. Outages only end up in the alert history.
monitor.disabledHint: A rule exists but is switched off.
monitor.noneHint: No alert rule watches this service yet.
monitor.createdHint: Assign it a channel under Alerts so that outages reach you.
monitor.noPermission: Monitoring runs through alert rules. You lack the permission for that.

repositories.lead: Templates for package sources. In the server detail under “Add repository” you pick one of them; LCM downloads the key and sets up the source to match the server's package manager.
repositories.caption: Known package sources

empty.title: No package source in the catalogue yet
empty.text: Create a template, for example for Docker or NodeSource. It then shows up for selection in the server detail.

form.name: Name
form.keyHint: Sets the file names on the server, e.g. /etc/apt/keyrings/<identifier>.asc.
form.keyInvalid: Lower-case letters, digits and hyphens only.
form.managerHint: The source is only offered to servers with this package manager.
form.keyUrlHint: https, as text (.asc or .gpg.key). LCM fills in $ID, $CODENAME and $ARCH on the server.
form.keyUrlHttps: The address must start with https://.
form.lineHint: One line, starting with “deb ”. $ID (distribution), $CODENAME and $ARCH are resolved on the server. Use https and signed-by with the key above.
form.lineUrl: Enter an http or https address.
form.unsafe: Quotes, backslashes and $( are not allowed.

urlHint.dnf: Address of a .repo file; it is downloaded to /etc/yum.repos.d/.
urlHint.zypper: Added with “zypper addrepo”, the key is imported automatically.
urlHint.pacman: Added as a section to /etc/pacman.conf; the key is imported and signed locally.
urlHint.apk: Added as a line to /etc/apk/repositories; a given key goes to /etc/apk/keys.

delete.label: Delete package source
delete.title: Delete “{name}” from the catalogue?
delete.message: The template is no longer offered in the server detail.

repositories.cachePointer: You manage the central package cache for APT on its own page.

aptCache.lead: A package cache (apt-cacher-ng) in your own network downloads every package from the internet only once and hands it to all servers. You connect servers with the server action or a group rule.
aptCache.caption: APT caches

empty.title: No APT cache yet
empty.text: Add an apt-cacher-ng, for example one per site. Rules and server actions then pick one of them.

form.name: Name
form.urlHint: Servers enter this address as their APT proxy. For https sources apt-cacher-ng needs “PassThroughPattern: .*”.
form.urlInvalid: Expected http(s)://host[:port] without spaces or quotes.
form.nameInvalid: Without quotation marks and line breaks.

delete.label: Remove cache
delete.title: Remove “{name}” from LCM?
delete.message: LCM no longer knows the cache. Nothing changes on the cache itself.

stats.title: Transfer
stats.hint: Values from the apt-cacher-ng report page. Whatever was delivered beyond what was downloaded is bandwidth saved.
stats.unavailable: No statistics right now: the service must be running and reachable for LCM.

connected.title: Connected servers
connected.intro: These servers fetch their packages through one of the caches.
connected.none: No server is connected to a cache right now.

disconnect.label: Disconnect
disconnect.help: Removes the APT proxy setting on this server. It then downloads packages directly from the repositories again. A group rule “Use APT cache” reconnects it at the next health check.
disconnect.title: Disconnect “{name}” from the APT cache?
disconnect.message: APT requests then go directly to the repositories again.
disconnect.policyValue: reconnects at the next health check

host.title: Service on the LCM host
host.notManaged: Restart and retention can only be set when apt-cacher-ng runs on the LCM host itself. Check and statistics above work for every cache.
host.restartHelp: Restarts apt-cacher-ng on the LCM host. Downloads currently running through the cache abort and start again on the next attempt.
host.restartMessage: The service is unreachable for a few seconds.
host.permanentOn: The nightly clean-up is off. The cache grows until you clean up by hand.
host.permanentOff: apt-cacher-ng removes packages at night that no server needs any more.
host.permanentDisableTitle: Switch the nightly clean-up back on?
host.runsOnValue: the LCM host, as a job

notice.disconnected: “{name}” is disconnected from the APT cache

aptCache.monitorIntro: LCM checks the caches every 30 minutes with the alert evaluation. The check also detects a foreign service on the port.
aptCache.otherCaches: The caches of scan and early warning are under Security.

empty.title: No application in the catalogue yet
empty.text: Add a profile so that LCM finds software that does not come from the package manager.

form.builtinHint: Built-in: LCM resets markers, version command and source to the shipped state at the next start. The switch and both actions stay. For your own detection create a new entry.
form.slugHint: Lower-case letters, digits, hyphen. Cannot be changed later.
form.slugInvalid: Starts with a letter, then lower-case letters, digits or hyphens (at most 40).
form.englishHint: Optional. If empty, the English interface shows the German text.
form.markersHint: One line per marker, “kind value”, the first match counts. Kinds: path (file or directory), unit (systemd service), bin (program in PATH), proc (running process).
form.markersRequired: At least one marker is needed.
form.markersFormat: Every line needs “kind value” with path, unit, bin or proc.
form.markersUnsafe: Values must not contain spaces or special characters such as ; | $ *.
form.versionCommandHint: {path} is the location found. Empty: LCM only reports that the application is present.
form.versionPatternHint: Regular expression, the first group is the version. Empty: the first non-empty line of the output.
form.patternInvalid: This is not a valid regular expression.
form.sourceHint: github:owner/repo for the latest release on GitHub, otherwise url:https://… with a pattern. Empty: no comparison.
form.actionHint: Both are custom actions. If the backup fails, the update does not run.
form.enabledOn: The scan looks for the markers on all servers and runs the version command there as root.
form.enabledOff: The entry is kept, the scan skips it. Previous findings disappear at the next scan.

confirm.saveMessage: At the next scan LCM checks the markers on every server and, where one matches, runs the version command there.
confirm.whereValue: every server on which a marker matches

delete.label: Remove application
delete.title: Remove “{name}” from the catalogue?
delete.message: The findings of this application on the servers disappear as well.

explainer.title: How LCM finds applications
explainer.intro: Software that does not come from the package manager is in no package list. A profile tells LCM how to recognise it and how to learn its version.
explainer.markers: File, service, program or process. The first match counts and gives the location.
explainer.version: The version command runs at the location, the pattern cuts out the number.
explainer.latest: LCM asks the source once per application, not per server, and then compares.
explainer.update: Backup and update are custom actions, so they run with permission checks and a job log.
explainer.root: Markers and version command run as root on all matching servers at every scan. Only enter what you would run yourself.

crowdsec.lead: CrowdSec detects attacks on your servers and blocks the attackers. When set up through the server action “Security tools”, a server registers with a central LAPI or with the CrowdSec Console.
crowdsec.lapisIntro: Self-hosted CrowdSec LAPIs that servers connect to, for example one per site or customer.
crowdsec.caption: CrowdSec LAPIs

empty.title: No LAPI yet
empty.text: Add a self-hosted LAPI. You then pick it when setting up CrowdSec on a server.

connected.title: Connected servers
connected.intro: According to their CrowdSec configuration these servers report to one of the LAPIs.
connected.none: No server reports to these LAPIs yet. To connect: server detail → Actions → Security tools, CrowdSec in “remote” mode.

console.title: CrowdSec Console
console.intro: With an enrollment key LCM registers servers with your console on app.crowdsec.net during setup.
console.hint: From app.crowdsec.net (cscli console enroll). LCM stores it encrypted and never shows it again.

form.name: Name
form.urlInvalid: Expected http(s)://host[:port] without spaces or quotes.
form.passwordRequired: A new LAPI needs the password.
form.hint: Create the machine on the LAPI server first (cscli machines add). The password is stored encrypted.

delete.label: Remove LAPI
delete.title: Remove “{name}” from LCM?
delete.message: LCM no longer knows the LAPI. Nothing changes on the LAPI or on the servers.

crowdsec.monitorIntro: Every 30 minutes, with the alert evaluation, LCM does a test login at every LAPI and reports outages.

kind.backupHelp: Backs up the LCM database and settings. Nothing happens on the servers.
kind.cleanupHelp: Deletes job logs older than the configured retention. Nothing happens on the servers.
kind.cveScanHelp: Reloads the vulnerability database and then checks the packages of all servers, except demo servers and those in maintenance.
kind.alertCheckHelp: Evaluates all alert rules and notifies through their channels when something fires.
kind.updateCheckHelp: Checks whether there is a new LCM version. Nothing is installed.

trigger.label: Run
trigger.groupHelp: Runs the active rules of this schedule now, one after another, on all servers of the group, without waiting for the next date. The result then shows up in the jobs.
trigger.unknownHelp: Starts this schedule now. The result then shows up in the jobs.

impact.reboot: yes, at least one rule reboots

empty.title: No schedules
empty.text: You create schedules in the server groups; system schedules come from the settings, for example for backups.

adminOnly.title: Administrators only
adminOnly.text: The system-wide overview is reserved for administrators who may manage the settings. With the rules permission you manage the schedules of your groups directly in the groups.

explainer.title: Schedules in LCM
explainer.intro: All schedules in one place, sorted by the next run.
explainer.group: belong to a server group and run its rules on all servers of the group. You edit them in the group.
explainer.system: come from the settings (backup, log clean-up, CVE scan) or are built in (alert evaluation, update check).
explainer.manual: “Run” starts a run immediately. The regular date stays.

empty.title: No custom action yet
empty.text: Create a list of commands, for example “Restart services”. You then pick it as a rule in server groups.

systemctl restart nginx

form.commandsRequired: At least one command is needed.

hints.diskCapacity: Fires as soon as a file system of a server is filled above the limit.

hints.securityCve: Fires when the CVE scan finds vulnerabilities from the chosen severity upwards on a server.
hints.failedUpdates: Fires when more updates are pending on a server than allowed. Whether LCM can act is reported by “Action failed”.
hints.actionFailed: Fires immediately when LCM can no longer act on a server (connection, package manager, rules, CVE scan) and gives the all-clear once it works again. While the error lasts, the rule reminds you at the interval of the cooldown.
hints.heartbeat: Fires when a server has not been heard from for longer than set.
hints.rebootRequired: Fires as soon as a server asks for a reboot itself after updates, for example for a new kernel.
hints.aptCacherDown: Fires when an APT cache from the settings does not answer on its report page. Checked once, not per server.
hints.crowdsecLapiDown: Fires when a CrowdSec LAPI from the settings does not answer or rejects the machine login. Checked once, not per server.
hints.deepScan: Fires when the last deep scan of a server reports warnings or asks for a reboot for the kernel.
hints.cveDbStale: Fires when the vulnerability database is older than 48 hours. An old database reports no error, it simply does not find new issues: that looks like “all safe”.
hints.backupStale: Fires when automatic backups are on but the latest one is older than two intervals or there is none yet. It measures the result, not single failed attempts.
hints.advisory: Reports open early-warning findings from the chosen severity upwards. Malicious packages always fire. Findings you acknowledge under Security no longer fire.

rules.title: How rules work
rules.intro: A rule says what should happen on all servers of the group. Every rule belongs to a trigger.
rules.scheduled: The rule runs at the cron time, together with the other rules of the schedule.
rules.enforce: Is checked at every connection and enforced only if the server deviates. Possible for firewall, APT cache, ACL setup and permission baseline.
rules.priorityBefore: If a server is in several groups, the group with the smaller
rules.priorityAfter: wins for firewall and APT cache. The other rule is not executed there. You see conflicts on the rule.
rules.order: Within a trigger, rules run from top to bottom. Drag them or use the arrows to change the order.

schedules.title: How schedules work
schedules.intro: A schedule runs its rules one after another on all servers of the group at the set time.
schedules.run: “Run now” starts the run immediately. Only active rules run.
schedules.spread: With a time window, servers start spread out instead of all at once. This relieves a shared APT cache, for example. A manual start ignores the window.
schedules.timezone: Times apply in the time zone of the LCM server.
schedules.rules: What a schedule does is determined by its rules. You maintain them on the Rules tab.

priority.title: Priority
priority.definition: If several groups define the same thing for the same server, the group with the smaller number wins. The default is 100, the system group has 1000.

enforce.title: Baseline rule
enforce.definition: A rule with a target state, such as a firewall. LCM checks it at every connection to the server and only steps in if the server deviates.

acl.title: ACL
acl.definition: Access lists for files and directories. Permission profiles with directory rights need them on the server.

firewall.sourcesHint: IPv4, IPv6 or networks like 10.0.0.0/24, separated by commas. Empty means all sources, otherwise only these addresses and the chosen allowlists.
firewall.sshFixed: The SSH port always stays open.

schedules.onText: The schedule runs at the set time.
schedules.offText: The schedule does not run by itself. You can still start it by hand.

run.label: Run now
run.help: Starts the schedule right now on all servers of the group. The active rules run one after another.
run.meaning: This is the same as the run at the cron time, only now and without the time window. You see the progress under Jobs.
run.title: Run schedule “{name}” now?
run.message: The rules run right away on all servers of the group.

impact.enforce: Is checked at every connection and enforced only on deviation.
impact.noServers: The group has no servers yet, so the rule has no effect for now.
impact.maybeReboot: Restarts only if the system asks for it.

security.label: Security updates
security.help: Installs only security and bugfix updates from the security sources.

packages.label: Update specific packages
packages.help: Updates only the packages you name.

packageScan.label: Refresh package list
packageScan.help: Reloads the package lists and records the inventory. Installs nothing.

autoremove.label: Remove unneeded packages
autoremove.help: Removes packages nothing needs any more (apt autoremove and equivalents).

rebootIfNeeded.label: Restart if needed
rebootIfNeeded.help: Restarts only if the system itself asks for a restart, otherwise the run is skipped.

dockerComposeUpdate.label: Docker: update compose projects
dockerComposeUpdate.help: Pulls new images, recreates the containers and removes old images.

dockerContainerUpdate.label: Docker: update standalone containers
dockerContainerUpdate.help: Pulls new images and recreates running containers with the same configuration.

dockerUpdateUnused.label: Docker: update unused images
dockerUpdateUnused.help: Pulls new versions of images no container uses.

dockerPrune.label: Docker: prune unused images
dockerPrune.help: Deletes unused Docker images (docker image prune -af).

deepScan.label: Deep scan
deepScan.help: Checks pending kernel restarts, kernel vulnerabilities and hardening. Read-only.

dnsTest.label: DNS test
dnsTest.help: Checks whether the test domains resolve on the server. Read-only.

sync.label: Sync users and hardware
sync.help: Syncs user certificates and hardware data.

firewall.label: Firewall
firewall.help: Keeps the firewall at the target state. SSH always stays open. The tool (ufw, firewalld, nftables) depends on the distribution.

aptProxy.label: Use APT cache
aptProxy.help: Connects the servers to the central APT cache. As a baseline rule the connection is restored if it deviates.

aclSetup.label: Set up ACL
aclSetup.help: Makes sure access lists are usable so directory rights from profiles take effect.

permSync.label: Keep permission baseline
permSync.help: Compares permissions with the baseline and steps in only on deviation.

script.label: Run script
script.help: Runs your own script as root.

custom.label: Custom action
custom.help: Runs a command list from the settings.

cveScan.label: CVE scan
cveScan.help: Looks for vulnerabilities in the package inventory of all servers.

dockerCheck.label: Docker check
dockerCheck.help: Checks registries for updates and images for vulnerabilities.

appCheck.label: Application check
appCheck.help: Asks for the latest version of every application in the catalog.

refresh.label: Refresh package list
refresh.help: Queries the package sources and re-reads the installed packages. Nothing is installed.
refresh.meaning: Afterwards you see which updates are available.

upgradeAll.label: Install all updates
upgradeAll.help: Installs every available update on this server. Services may be restarted in the process.
upgradeAll.meaning: Affected services are briefly unavailable. A reboot may be needed afterwards.

upgradeSecurity.label: Security updates only
upgradeSecurity.help: Installs only the updates that close security holes. Everything else stays as it is.
upgradeSecurity.meaning: Services may restart; feature updates wait until you install them.

autoremove.label: Remove unneeded packages
autoremove.help: Removes packages that were only installed as dependencies and are no longer needed.
autoremove.meaning: Disk space is freed. Removed packages can be installed again.

kernels.label: Remove old kernels
kernels.help: Removes kernels that are not running and not needed as a fallback.
kernels.meaning: The running kernel and a fallback are kept.

updateSelected.label: Update selected
updateSelected.help: Updates exactly the selected packages to the available version.
updateSelected.meaning: Only these packages change; dependent services may restart.

removeSelected.label: Remove selected
removeSelected.help: Uninstalls the selected packages. The server rejects protected system packages.
removeSelected.meaning: Programs that need the package stop working afterwards.

freeze.help: Holds {package} at the installed version so that an update does not jump to an affected version by accident.

advisory.title: Early warning queries (OSV)
advisory.intro: How many packages were answered from the cache instead of asking the online source.

advisory.tune: Adjust the validity in the settings

exposed.title: Exposed packages
exposed.definition: Packages from the list in the settings and packages of services that LCM detected listening on a port. An attack from outside hits them first.

cve.title: How to read the findings
cve.intro: All servers are checked centrally every day with Trivy against the vulnerability database. Critical findings turn the affected server red.
cve.container: Findings in container images count one level lower for the traffic light and alerts, because containers run isolated.
cve.exposed: findings in them count one level higher.
cve.raw: The table shows the raw rating, not the weighted one.
cve.bulk: The bulk update installs the security updates on every reachable server, one after the other.

advisories.title: Early warning and scan
advisories.intro: Early warning regularly compares the package inventory with the online source OSV. It is the fast track next to the daily scan.
advisories.fast: Findings are minutes old, not a day.
advisories.malware: It knows advisories about malicious packages that the Trivy database does not carry at all.
advisories.noFix: If there is no fixed version yet, you can freeze the installed one.
advisories.ack: If you acknowledge a finding, it stays visible but no longer raises an alert.

caches.title: What are the caches for?
caches.intro: They show how often a question was already answered instead of causing work again. The two caches measure different things and cannot be combined into one number.
caches.reading: A low rate is not a flaw: with very different servers there is simply little to repeat. It only becomes meaningful over several runs.

instances.intro: The inventory comes from the Docker check and shows what was running at the last survey.
instances.stopped: Exited containers are often intentional and therefore only appear in the list on request.
instances.symptoms: “Restarting” and “Dead” are symptoms and show in red.

compose.title: How to read the projects
compose.intro: Containers with a Compose label are grouped into projects across all servers. If a project runs on several servers, all of them are listed.
compose.incomplete: If not every container of a project is running, the row carries a warning: usually the reason to look here.

profile.definition: A privilege profile defines what a Linux user may do on a server: single commands as root, single files to edit, rights on directories. On the server it becomes a group lcm-prof-<slug> with its own sudoers file.

block.title: Rule block
block.definition: A ready-made rights template you add to profiles, such as “restart a service”. It brings the right commands for each Linux family and has placeholders like {service} that the profile fills in.

access.title: Server groups
access.intro: A group gives the user access to all of its servers. You can choose a different profile per group.
access.noGroups: Not assigned to any group yet.
access.aclIncomplete: Only {ok} of {total} servers in this group support ACLs. The profile's directory rights have no effect there - install the “acl” package on those servers.

assign.label: Assign
assign.help: Assigns the user to the group. LCM creates the account on all servers of the group right away, distributes the SSH keys and applies the chosen profile's rights.
assign.meaning: The user can then log in on these servers.
assign.heading: Assign “{group}”?
assign.effect: Create account, distribute SSH keys, apply profile rights.

change.heading: Change profile for “{group}”?
change.message: “{profile}” then applies on the servers of this group.
change.effect: The user's sudo and directory rights are replaced during the sync.

remove.label: Remove from group
remove.help: Removes the user from the group. LCM deletes the account including its home directory on the group's servers where the user has no other access.
remove.meaning: Data in the home directory on these servers is gone afterwards.
remove.heading: Remove from “{group}”?
remove.effect: Account and home directory are deleted on these servers.

sync.label: Sync now
sync.help: Syncs the Linux users on all of this user's servers right away: accounts, keys and rights are brought in line with LCM.
sync.meaning: Needed, for example, after a change to a profile or block, which otherwise only takes effect at the next sync.
sync.heading: Sync the servers of “{name}”?
sync.effect: All Linux users on these servers are brought in line with LCM.

keys.title: SSH keys
keys.empty: No keys yet. Without a key the user can only log in with a password.
keys.name: Label
keys.invalid: This does not look like a public SSH key (ssh-ed25519, ssh-rsa, ecdsa-…).

add.label: Add key
add.help: Stores the public key and distributes it to all of the user's servers right away.
add.meaning: Whoever holds the matching private key can then log in as this user.
add.effect: The key goes into the account's authorized_keys.

generate.label: Generate key pair
generate.help: LCM generates a new key pair, stores the public part and distributes it to all of the user's servers. You get the private key once to download.
generate.meaning: LCM does not store the private key. If you close the window first, it is gone.
generate.effect: The new public key goes into the account's authorized_keys.

remove.label: Remove key
remove.help: Deletes the key and removes it from all of the user's servers right away.
remove.meaning: Logging in with this key no longer works afterwards.

activation.mailFailed: The link was created, but sending failed: {error}. Copy it and pass it on yourself.

profiles.blocksHint: Ready-made templates instead of hand-written rules. A block brings the right lines for each Linux family; you fill placeholders such as the service name here.
profiles.sudoHint: Full command line with an absolute path. sudo compares the whole line: “/usr/bin/systemctl restart nginx” allows exactly that, “/usr/bin/systemctl” alone allows practically everything.
profiles.requirePasswordOn: sudo asks for the user's password before the command.
profiles.requirePasswordOff: The command runs without a password prompt, also from scripts.
profiles.rootEquivalentOn: You confirm: this command can give full root rights (such as a shell or an editor). LCM accepts it as is.
profiles.rootEquivalentOff: LCM rejects commands that recognisably give full root rights.
profiles.editHint: Files the user may edit as root. sudoedit starts the editor without root rights and writes the file back afterwards - nobody gets a root shell out of the editor.
profiles.pathsHint: Additional rights on single directories, set via POSIX ACLs. System directories are blocked.

error.slugInvalid: Lowercase letters, digits and hyphen, at most 20 characters.
error.commandRelative: The command needs an absolute path, such as /usr/bin/systemctl.

error.paramName: Placeholders: lowercase letters, digits and _, separated by commas.
error.noRules: The block needs at least one variant with a rule.
error.pathLine: One “right path” per line, right is read, readwrite or deny, the path absolute.

profiles.caption: Privilege profiles

form.accountHint: With “File access only” the account gets no shell: login via SFTP only. Visible is what the directory rights allow.

delete.label: Delete profile

explainer.assign: It is assigned on the user: as the default profile or per server group.
explainer.blocks: Rule blocks save you from writing single rules.
explainer.builtin: Built-in profiles can only be copied, not changed.
explainer.written: a group lcm-prof-<slug>, the sudoers file /etc/sudoers.d/lcm-prof-<slug> and ACLs for the directory rights. For those the server needs the “acl” package.

variant.commands: Commands as root, one per line
variant.files: Files to edit, one per line
variant.pathsHint: Format “right path”, right is read, readwrite or deny. Works via ACLs; without the “acl” package on the server the sync reports it.

activate.title: Set your password
activate.intro: Set the password for your LCM account. The link is valid only briefly and only once.
activate.resetIntro: Set a new password for your LCM account. Afterwards only the new one works and all sign-ins with the old one end.
activate.done: The password is saved. You can sign in now.
activate.doneAs: The password is saved. You can now sign in as {username}.

linuxActivate.intro: Choose how you sign in to the Linux servers: with a password, an SSH key or both. The link works only once.
linuxActivate.noToken: The address is missing the key from the invitation. Open the link completely or ask for a new one.
linuxActivate.passwordText: Optional if you add an SSH key. Used for signing in and for sudo on the servers.
linuxActivate.keyText: With a key you sign in without a password – safer and more convenient.

key.label: Key
key.noneText: Sign in with the password only.
key.pasteText: You only hand out the public part; the private one stays on your machine.
key.generateText: Convenient: you download the private key once right afterwards.
key.name: Label
key.publicKeyHint: Contents of the .pub file, one line, e.g. from ~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub.
key.invalid: This does not look like an OpenSSH public key (type, key, optionally a name).
key.generateNote: LCM creates an ed25519 key pair. You get the private key exactly once, right after setting up – LCM stores it nowhere.

linuxActivate.done: Saved. At the next sync LCM sets up access for {username} on the assigned servers; then you can sign in there.
linuxActivate.copyFailed: Copying failed – download the file instead.

privateKey.title: Your private key
privateKey.text: Download it now. It exists only on this page and is gone once you leave – LCM keeps no copy.

joinWizard.title: Add server
joinWizard.forbidden: Only users who may manage servers (servers:write) can add servers.

problem.host: Host name or IP address only, without scheme or path.

mode.label: Connection type
mode.sshText: LCM connects to the server. It needs an address LCM can reach.
mode.agentText: The server connects to LCM – behind NAT, without a fixed IP, on the road.
mode.routerosText: Watches whether the RouterOS version is current.
mode.dsmText: Watches DSM, packages, volumes and the Security Advisor through the web API.

ssh.loginUserHint: root or a user who can become root. LCM finds the way itself: sudo (with or without password) or su.
ssh.passwordHint: Leave empty if the user gets in without a password – LCM then tries a passwordless sign-in.
ssh.keyHint: LCM signs in with its system SSH key. Put its public part into ~/.ssh/authorized_keys of the login user on the target server first.
ssh.keyWhere: Users who may manage settings find the public key under Settings → General.

restricted.label: Restricted rights (recommended)
restricted.description: The LCM user may only manage packages, Docker and the firewall and read the system.
restricted.on: On: no shell or file system access for LCM. In return SSH hardening, custom repositories, APT cache and custom scripts are locked for this server.
restricted.off: Off: LCM gets passwordless sudo for everything and can use all features.

ssh.duplicate: This address with this port already exists:
ssh.sameHost: There already is a server at this address on port {port} (allowed, e.g. behind NAT):
ssh.fingerprintVerify: Cross-check on the target server (at the console):
ssh.fingerprintHint: If the value does not match the server, someone could be intercepting the connection – cancel here in that case. LCM remembers this key and refuses to connect if it ever changes.

does.login: Signs in once with your login user and becomes root (sudo or su).
does.user: Creates the service user lcm-svc and installs a key LCM generates for this server only.
does.reuser: Recreates the service user lcm-svc and installs a new key generated for this server only.
does.sudoRestricted: Gives lcm-svc only the rights for package management, Docker, firewall and reading the system.
does.verify: Checks the sign-in with the new key and reads the system: packages, sources, users, containers, storage.
does.group: Adds the server to the system group – so health checks and sync run right away.
does.keep: The server's groups and user assignments stay, the old credentials are replaced.

ssh.passwordNotStored: LCM uses the login password only for this setup and does not store it. The new key is stored encrypted.
ssh.noHardening: LCM does not change SSH itself here. You can harden it later (root login, password sign-in) with the server actions.

run.label: Add server now
run.help: LCM signs in to the server with your details, sets up the service user lcm-svc with its own key and sudo rights and reads the system.
run.meaning: Afterwards LCM manages the server; this usually takes less than a minute.

ssh.doneJob: The complete output of the setup is in the job at the server.

reconnect.title: Reconnect server
reconnect.intro: Reconnects to {name} – for example after the credentials changed or the server was replaced.
reconnect.notFound: This server does not exist or you may not see it.
reconnect.onlySsh: Only servers LCM reaches via SSH can be reconnected.
reconnect.fingerprintHint: If the server was replaced, it has a new host key – that is expected then. Otherwise: if the value does not match, someone could be intercepting the connection. Cancel in that case.

run.label: Reconnect now
run.help: LCM signs in with your details, recreates the service user lcm-svc with a new key and replaces the stored credentials.
run.meaning: Groups and user assignments stay as they are.

rootGuide.title: Root login via SSH is locked? How to open it briefly
rootGuide.intro: Many distributions do not let root in via SSH. Simpler: use a sudo user as login user, then you need none of this. Otherwise:
rootGuide.console: Sign in at the server console (VM or cloud console) – root cannot get in via SSH yet.
rootGuide.password: If root has no password yet, set one:
rootGuide.allow: Allow root login in a separate file that can be removed cleanly later:
rootGuide.allowOld: Older systems without {dir}: set the line {line} in {file} (change an existing line, do not add a second one).
rootGuide.join: Add the server here with login user root and this password.
rootGuide.after: Close it again afterwards: LCM no longer needs the root login once the server is added. Remove the file and restart SSH – or use the server action “Block root login”.

agent.nameHint: Only the display name – the agent handles address and access itself.
agent.readyTitle: {name} has been created – now install the agent
agent.once: The token is shown only now. LCM stores only a hash; if it gets lost, generate a new one at the server.
agent.repoHint: Sets up the Techeve package source with its signing key – not needed if it is already there.
agent.enroll: 3. Connect to LCM and start as a service
agent.enrollHint: The token is valid for this server only.
agent.portHint: The token is valid for this server only. The agent connects on port {port}; the server must be able to reach it.
agent.manualLabel: Load the agent directly from LCM and connect
agent.manualHint: Downloads the program from this LCM (-k: self-signed certificate, the agent pins it afterwards through the token). For ARM64 servers replace amd64 with arm64.
agent.after: Once connected the server goes online and the first scan starts by itself.

routeros.userHint: A RouterOS user with SSH access, ideally read-only, e.g. admin.
routeros.passwordHint: In the factory state admin has no password – leave it empty then.
routeros.keyModeHint: LCM creates a key pair; you import the public key on the router afterwards. Until then the device stays offline.
routeros.keyReadyHint: Put the public key on the router as file lcm.pub (e.g. drag and drop in WinBox) and import it. The next sync then connects.

dsm.accountHint: An account of the administrators group, ideally only for LCM and without enforced two-factor sign-in (an unattended scan cannot enter a code).
dsm.fingerprintHint: DSM ships with a self-signed certificate. LCM remembers this fingerprint and refuses to connect if it ever changes. Compare it in DSM under Control Panel → Security → Certificate. Only after this confirmation are the credentials sent to the device.

ssh.intro: On the server LCM works with its own service user and its own key, not with your login.
ssh.fingerprint: First LCM reads the server's host key – without credentials yet. You confirm it; from then on LCM checks exactly this key on every connection.
ssh.login: Then LCM signs in once with your login and becomes root.
ssh.user: It creates lcm-svc, installs a key generated for this server only and grants sudo rights – full or restricted.
ssh.scan: Finally it checks the sign-in with the new key and reads the system.
ssh.notDone: Not included: changes to the SSH configuration. You can harden it later step by step; every change shows a command preview at its action.

reconnect.intro: Reconnecting replaces LCM's credentials; the server stays the same.
reconnect.user: LCM recreates the service user lcm-svc.
reconnect.key: It generates a new key for this server only and replaces the old one.
reconnect.keep: Groups, schedules and user assignments stay unchanged.

agent.intro: With the agent the server opens the connection itself – LCM does not need to reach it.
agent.outbound: The agent connects outbound (MQTT over WebSocket to LCM's agent port); no port forwarding needed at the server.
agent.token: The token binds the agent to exactly this server. LCM shows it once and stores only a hash.
agent.after: As soon as the agent is connected the server goes online and the first scan runs.

routeros.intro: RouterOS has no package management like Linux. LCM only watches the device.
routeros.watch: It reports when a newer RouterOS version is available.
routeros.limits: Firewall rules, CVE scan, repositories and user sync are not available here.
routeros.user: A read-only user is enough; LCM changes nothing on the router.

dsm.intro: DSM manages packages, users and services itself. That is why LCM talks to the DSM web API instead of setting the device up like a Linux server.
dsm.watch: It watches DSM version and updates, packages, volumes, time and the Security Advisor findings.
dsm.cert: No SSH, no service user: instead of the host key you confirm the DSM certificate.
dsm.account: In DSM you can additionally restrict the LCM account to LCM's IP address.

password.mismatch: The two entries do not match.
password.requirements: At least 12 characters from at least three kinds (upper case, lower case, digits, symbols); from 20 characters two kinds are enough. Not allowed: your name, well-known default passwords, number or keyboard sequences.

problem.whitespace_edges: Must not start or end with a space.
problem.needs_classes: More variety needed: at least three kinds of upper case, lower case, digits and symbols (two from 20 characters).
problem.contains_identity: Contains your user name, name or part of your email address.
problem.context_word: Consists mainly of an obvious word such as “admin”, “password” or “lcm”.
problem.sequence: Contains a predictable sequence such as “1234”, “abcd” or “qwerty”.

required.passwordText: Your account needs a new password before you can continue. Afterwards you sign in once more and land where you wanted to go.
required.twoFactorText: Two-factor sign-in is required for your role. Set it up now, then you continue where you wanted to go.

profile.emailHint: LCM sends password reset links to this address.
profile.currentPasswordHint: A new address will receive the reset links from now on – that is why you need your password for it.
profile.passwordMissing: Enter your current password to change the email address.

password.title: Change password
password.subtitle: Afterwards you sign in again everywhere.

twoFactor.noScanner: No scanner? Enter the key by hand
twoFactor.codeMissing: Enter the six-digit code from your app.

confirm.label: Turn off

impact.policyValue: Then LCM locks everything else until you set it up again
impact.reversibleValue: Yes, by setting it up again

preferences.languageSubtitle: Applies to your account on all devices.

theme.label: Colour scheme

density.label: Density

density.compactText: More rows at a glance, for example in large server lists.

console.body:
This console is for developers. Anyone asking you to paste or type something here wants to take over your LCM session, and with it root access to every managed server.

If you do not know exactly what a command does: paste nothing, close this window.

reload.text: LCM was updated. The page reloads in a moment.

update.backup: Backup running, then LCM {version} will be installed.
update.installing: Installing LCM {version}. The page reloads afterwards.

confirm.title: Install LCM {version}?

impact.backupValue: Database backup, no update without it

docker.updatesOffHelp: Docker updates are switched off for this server in its settings. The inventory is still read; pull and compose update are blocked.

pullAll.help: Pulls the latest version of every used, tagged image from its registry (one job). Running containers keep the old image until they are recreated; update Compose projects afterwards with “Update project”.
pullAll.heading: Update all images on {name}?

refresh.label: Re-read inventory
refresh.help: Reads containers and images again (docker ps, docker images). Changes nothing on the server.

projectUpdate.label: Update project
projectUpdate.help: Pulls new images for {project} and recreates the project's containers (docker compose pull && up -d). The services are briefly down.

serviceUpdate.label: Update
serviceUpdate.help: Pulls the new image for {target} and recreates only this service. It is briefly down.

docker.standaloneHint: Without Compose LCM cannot recreate them losslessly: pull the image below and recreate the container yourself.
docker.noContainersText: Re-read the inventory if containers should be running here.

empty.title: No containers
empty.text: No containers or images are recorded on this server. Re-read the inventory if that is wrong.

pull.label: Pull
pull.help: Fetches the latest version of {image} (docker pull). Running containers keep the old image until they are recreated.
pull.heading: Pull {image} again?

remove.heading: Delete {image}?

prune.heading: Clean up unused images on {name}?

relevant.on: Vulnerabilities in this container's image count at full severity in the server's status.
relevant.off: Container image vulnerabilities don't count in the status by default; they are only listed here and under Security.
relevant.onDone: Vulnerabilities of {name} now count in the status
relevant.offDone: Vulnerabilities of {name} no longer count in the status

pull.label: Update
pull.help: Pulls the latest version of {image} on every server that has it (docker pull, one job per server).
pull.meaning: Running containers keep the old image until they are recreated.
pull.heading: Update {image} everywhere?

compose.label: Update
compose.help: Pulls new images for {project} and recreates the containers on every server with this project (one job per server).
compose.meaning: The project's services are briefly down.
compose.heading: Update Compose project {project} everywhere?

refresh.label: Re-read
refresh.help: Reads the accounts that can log in again over SSH. Changes nothing on the server.

pending.hint: The server was unreachable on the last attempt. LCM catches up as soon as it answers again.

empty.title: No accounts recorded
empty.text: LCM reads the server's accounts that can log in. Re-read them if some should be listed here.

enable.label: Unlock
enable.help: Unlocks the account {name}: password and expiry are reset, logins work again.
enable.heading: Unlock {name}?

disable.help: Locks {name} on this server: password locked, account expired, key logins stop working too. Reversible.
disable.helpManaged: Locks {name} on this server only. The user stays assigned in LCM and usable on other servers; the next sync does not lift the lock.
disable.heading: Lock {name}?

logins.sourceLcm: This account logs in without a terminal, which the system does not record. These logins come from LCM's own session log.

install.label: Install tools
install.help: Installs needrestart and lynis on the server. With them the scan finds outdated services and checks hardening thoroughly.
install.meaning: Two packages are added to the server; the configuration stays as it is.
install.heading: Install scan tools on {name}?

deepScan.kernelReboot: The running kernel is older than the installed one. Only a reboot makes the kernel security fixes take effect.
deepScan.noKernelCves: The last scan found no kernel-related vulnerabilities.
deepScan.noReports: No run yet. Start the scan and the first report appears here.

monitor.on: LCM warns as soon as usage reaches the threshold, as it does for /.
monitor.off: Display only. An archive may fill up; an alert about it would be noise.

version.title: Choose a version of {name}
version.none: The package manager offers no other version (or this is a demo server).

install.label: Install
install.heading: Install {name} {version}?
install.help: Installs exactly this version of {name}, including an older one. Runs as a job; services using the package restart.

pins.title: Package pins
pins.subtitle: Protect packages from cleanup
pins.openHelp: Pinned packages survive cleanup and can be frozen at their version. Mainly for older kernels: they are the fallback when a new one does not boot.
pins.empty: No pins yet: cleanup currently removes older kernels too.
pins.proxmox: Not used on Proxmox: Proxmox keeps kernels itself. A second protection list would work against it.

kernel.label: Protect kernels
kernel.help: Adds this package manager's kernel patterns as pins ({patterns}) so several kernels are kept. Changes nothing on the server yet.
kernel.done: Kernels protected: older kernels are kept

apply.label: Apply on the server
apply.heading: Apply pins on {name}?
apply.help: Writes the pins to the server: protection files against cleanup and frozen versions. Until then new pins only take effect at the next cleanup. Runs as a job.

remove.label: Remove pin
remove.heading: Remove the pin “{name}”?
remove.effectValue: The package can be cleaned up again

new.title: New pin
new.name: Package or pattern
new.nameHint: A trailing * matches every package with this prefix.
new.noRemoveOn: Cleanup leaves the package in place.
new.holdOn: The package gets no more updates.
new.globalOn: The pin applies to all servers, not just this one.
new.holdWarn: Frozen means no more security updates. Dangerous for kernels.
new.nameInvalid: Only letters, digits and . _ + -, with a * at the end as wildcard.

revert.heading: Revert package sources on {name} to HTTP?

add.heading: Set up {repo} on {name}?
add.help: Sets up the source from the catalog: the signing key is fetched and the source added as signed. Then you can install its packages.
add.noCatalog: The catalog (Settings → Repositories) has no source for this server's package manager.
add.proxmox: Proxmox manages its package sources itself.

cache.title: APT cache
cache.none: No APT cache set up (Settings → APT cache).

connect.label: Use APT cache
connect.heading: Connect {name} to the APT cache?
connect.help: Routes all package downloads of this server through the central APT cache. Saves bandwidth when several servers fetch the same packages.
connect.done: {name} now fetches packages through the APT cache

disconnect.label: Disconnect APT cache
disconnect.heading: Disconnect {name} from the APT cache?
disconnect.help: The server fetches packages directly from the sources again. LCM removes its APT setting on the server.

unknown.title: Unassigned
unknown.subtitle: Running services whose unit file belongs to no package
unknown.empty: Every running service belongs to a package.

settings.title: Server settings
settings.name: Name
settings.connectionNote: Only changes where LCM connects to. Change the SSH port on the server under Access.

invalid.name: Enter a name.
invalid.nameFormat: At most 64 characters, no control characters.
invalid.hostFormat: Hostname or IP address, at most 253 characters.

maintenance.label: In maintenance
maintenance.on: On: LCM leaves the server alone – no schedules, checks, scans or alerts. For systems that are off on purpose.
maintenance.off: Off: The server is monitored normally; if it is off, it counts as faulty.
maintenance.short: No schedules, checks, scans or alerts.

unreachable_uncritical.label: Unreachability not critical
unreachable_uncritical.on: On: An unreachable server keeps its last state and only turns red after the grace period.
unreachable_uncritical.off: Off: An unreachable server turns critical at once.
unreachable_uncritical.short: An unreachable server only turns red after a grace period.

grace.label: Grace period (days)
grace.hint: After {days} days without connection the server turns red.

user_sync_disabled.label: Do not sync Linux users
user_sync_disabled.on: On: LCM creates no users here and distributes no SSH keys. Assignments stay saved.
user_sync_disabled.off: Off: LCM syncs this server's users with its groups.
user_sync_disabled.short: LCM creates no users here and distributes no SSH keys.

docker_updates_disabled.label: Do not apply Docker updates
docker_updates_disabled.on: On: LCM applies no new image versions here, neither by hand nor by rule. Updates are still shown.
docker_updates_disabled.off: Off: LCM may update container images.
docker_updates_disabled.short: LCM applies no new image versions here.

docker_cves_ignored.label: Ignore vulnerabilities in container images
docker_cves_ignored.on: On: Findings from images do not count for status, alerts and the security overview. They stay in the CVE report.
docker_cves_ignored.note: This also applies to containers marked CVE-relevant or reachable past the firewall.
docker_cves_ignored.short: Findings from images do not count for status and alerts.

console_disabled.label: Disable console
console_disabled.on: On: The console is gone from the server page and direct calls are refused.
console_disabled.off: Off: Anyone with the permission can open a console here.
console_disabled.short: The console is gone from the server page.

deny.label: Block root login
deny.heading: Block root login on {name}?
deny.help: root can no longer log in directly via SSH (PermitRootLogin no). LCM logs in with its own user and is not affected.

allow.label: Allow root login
allow.heading: Allow root login on {name} again?
allow.help: root may log in directly via SSH again. That opens a popular attack target.

apply.label: Change port
apply.heading: Change the SSH port on {name}?
apply.help: sshd then listens on the new port, and LCM only connects through it. Adjust clients and scripts that use the old port.

dns.title: Name servers

apply.label: Apply DNS
apply.heading: Change the name servers on {name}?
apply.help: Sets up to three name servers on the server. Leaving all fields empty hands DNS management back.

dns.note: Sets up to four name servers on the server: as a drop-in with systemd-resolved, otherwise in /etc/resolv.conf. Leaving all fields empty hands DNS management back.
