time.container: Container ({type}): The clock comes from the host. A time service does not start here; set up syncing on the host.

check.label: Check time
check.help: Reads the time zone, time service and clock offset fresh from the server. Changes nothing there.

setZone.label: Set time zone
setZone.heading: Change the time zone on {name}?
setZone.help: Changes the server's time zone. The clock itself stays correct; schedules (cron) and logs then show the new local time.

ntp.label: Set up time servers
ntp.heading: Set up time servers on {name}?
ntp.help: Sets the time servers, starts the time service and checks that the clock is in sync. A wrong clock breaks TLS, logs and one-time passwords.

time.invalidZone: Time zone in IANA format, such as Europe/Berlin.

settings.nameHint: Only the display name in LCM, must be unique across servers; the hostname on the server stays as it is.
settings.hostHint: LCM will connect here via SSH and checks the stored host key; if a different machine answers, the connection is refused (then use “Reconnect”).

clock.label: Clock
clock.container: Container ({type}): the clock comes from the host and can only be set there.

facts.kernelNewerHint: A newer kernel is installed but only runs after a reboot.
facts.kernelFromHost: Container ({type}): the kernel comes from the host and cannot be managed here.
facts.kexPqHint: Recorded traffic stays protected even against a future quantum computer.
facts.kexClassicHint: Secure today, but recorded traffic would be readable for a future quantum computer. Fix: OpenSSH 9.9 or newer on the server.

kernels.title: Installed kernels
kernels.unknownRunning: The running kernel ({release}) belongs to no installed package, probably a custom build or third-party source.

lcmHost.title: LCM host
lcmHost.intro: LCM itself runs on this server. Set up the services LCM uses here.
lcmHost.inContainer: LCM runs in a container. There is neither apt nor a service that survives a restart; in container mode Trivy runs as its own service. Add the Docker host itself like any other server via its network address.
lcmHost.notApt: Automatic setup is only available on Debian and Ubuntu (apt).

trivy.sandboxOffHint: The scanner runs with LCM's rights and could reach its data directory. Only the bubblewrap package is missing.
trivy.label: Set up Trivy
trivy.help: Adds the Aqua Security package archive, installs Trivy and then enables CVE scanning. Runs as a job on this server.
trivy.meaning: LCM then scans all servers for known vulnerabilities.
trivy.name: Trivy

sandbox.label: Add sandbox
sandbox.help: Installs bubblewrap. LCM then confines Trivy on every call, without a restart. Trivy itself stays unchanged.
sandbox.meaning: The scanner can no longer reach LCM's database and keys.

aptCacher.label: Set up apt-cacher-ng
aptCacher.help: Installs apt-cacher-ng on this server and enters it as package cache in the settings. Managed servers then download packages from the internet only once.
aptCacher.meaning: Updates are faster and save bandwidth.
aptCacher.name: apt-cacher-ng

lapi.label: Set up CrowdSec LAPI
lapi.help: Sets up the CrowdSec LAPI server on this server and enters the credentials in the CrowdSec settings. Managed servers can then connect in remote mode. The bouncer also enforces bans in this server's firewall.
lapi.meaning: Managed servers then share one ban list.
lapi.name: CrowdSec LAPI

groups.title: Groups
groups.noneExist: There are no groups yet. Create them under Groups.

harden.label: Harden SSH
harden.hint: Turn off password login and root login by password

unharden.hint: Restore the SSH settings from before hardening

rotateKey.label: Renew key
rotateKey.effect: The old key is removed from the server.

agentToken.label: Renew agent token
agentToken.effect: The agent connection drops until the agent is enrolled with the new token.
agentToken.title: New agent token
agentToken.once: The token is shown only now. LCM stores only a hash of it.

reboot.downtime: until the server is back up

unrestrict.label: Restore full rights
unrestrict.title: Restore full rights
unrestrict.intro: LCM cannot lift restricted mode itself; its access deliberately lacks the rights. Log in to the server directly and run:
unrestrict.warn: The commands give the LCM user full root rights again and remove the whitelist and LCM helper.
unrestrict.after: Then run “Reconnect” here without restricted rights.

restrictInfo.intro: The LCM user on this server currently has full root rights. This action restricts it to a fixed whitelist, exactly like the “Restricted rights” option during onboarding.
restrictInfo.allowed: Via sudo only: manage packages (apt/dnf/zypper, snap), Docker and the ufw firewall and read the system, plus, through the bundled, strictly validating LCM helper: set up repositories, connect the APT cache, configure SSH (hardening, root login, port) and synchronize Linux users.
restrictInfo.blocked: No arbitrary commands via LCM: custom scripts, custom actions and reboot are disabled for this server, as is invoking a root shell directly.
restrictInfo.scopeLabel: What this protects against, and what it does not
restrictInfo.scope: The mode reduces the attack surface against operating mistakes and accidental changes. It does not protect against someone who obtains the service key: package management and Docker run code as root by design (for example through apt hooks or containers mounting the host), and sudo cannot reliably filter their arguments. Without those programs the mode would be pointless, because updates and Docker are exactly what should keep working.
restrictInfo.irreversibleLabel: Cannot be undone with a click
restrictInfo.irreversible: Afterwards the LCM user itself no longer has the rights to grant itself root again. Going back works via “Reconnect” (with the login password) or manually on the server; the instructions appear in the actions menu afterwards.

tips.syncUsers: Distributes the Linux users managed in LCM to this server now: missing accounts and keys are added, locks are applied – without waiting for the next sync.
tips.rotateKey: Creates a new SSH key pair for LCM, installs it on the server, tests the login and then revokes the old key.
tips.reconnect: Opens the wizard to set up LCM's access again – for example after a reinstall or a new host key.
tips.dnsTest: Checks on the server whether the configured test domains resolve. The result then shows in the hardware block; nothing changes on the server.

abort.label: Abort job
abort.heading: Abort “{job}”?
abort.message: The connection is closed and the lock released.
abort.effectValue: Steps already run stay in place
abort.done: Job aborted, the server is free again

backup.label: Back up
backup.heading: Back up {name}
backup.help: Creates a backup of {name} on the server. Runs as a job; the app itself is not changed.

update.label: Update
update.heading: Update {name}
update.help: Updates {name} with the app's own updater, backing up first where the app supports it. Runs as a job on the server.

bar.refreshAllHelp: Reads everything from the server again: hardware, network and time, packages and updates, snaps, repositories, containers, plus disk usage and the state of firewall and SSH hardening. Runs as a job and changes nothing on the server.

serverSecurity.restricted: This server runs with restricted sudo. LCM needs full sudo access for these settings.

firewall.title: Firewall of {name}
firewall.lead: When enabled, everything not allowed here is blocked. SSH (port {port}) always stays open so you don't lock yourself out.
firewall.willInstall: will be set up when enabled
firewall.proxmox: Proxmox ships its own firewall (pve-firewall). LCM does not set up a second one here.

ssh.lockout: {ip} is missing. LCM reaches the server through this address; without it you lock LCM out.

listening.title: Listening services
listening.none: No listening services known yet. Query them from the server.
listening.covered: All listening services are allowed or run via SSH or Docker.

docker.title: Published by Docker, bypassing the firewall: {ports}
docker.hint: Docker adds these forwards to the packet filter itself. A rule here changes nothing. If a port must not be reachable from outside, bind it to 127.0.0.1 in the container (e.g. “127.0.0.1:8080:80”).

confirm.message: Afterwards only what is allowed is reachable.

disable.label: Disable
disable.heading: Disable the firewall on {name}?
disable.message: Afterwards the server no longer filters connections.

impact.lcmValue: locked out, {ip} is missing from the SSH sources

install.title: Set up security tools
install.submitHelp: Installs and configures the selected tool on this server.
install.lead: The address LCM uses to reach the server is already on the allowlist so LCM does not lock itself out.
install.fail2ban: Bans addresses after repeated failed logins.
install.crowdsec: Detects attacks in the logs and bans the attackers.
install.twoFactor: One-time code in addition to the SSH key.
install.allowlistHint: Separated by spaces or commas. Selected allowlists are added.

bouncer.label: Firewall bouncer
bouncer.off: CrowdSec only detects attacks, nothing gets banned.

lapi.label: Connection
lapi.remoteText: Reports to a LAPI from the settings.
lapi.consoleText: Reports to the console from the settings.
lapi.missing: Not set up yet in the CrowdSec settings.

twoFactor.title: SSH 2FA
twoFactor.intro: SSH logins ask for a one-time code from an authenticator app in addition to the key. Anyone who has not set up a code yet still gets in with the key alone. LCM's own access is exempt.
twoFactor.installWarn: Afterwards every SSH login with a configured code asks for it, and password-only logins stop working. Open sessions stay: set up your own code before you log out.
twoFactor.enroll: Everyone sets up their own code: run google-authenticator on the server and scan the QR code. Who has done so is shown in the tab

remove.label: Remove 2FA
remove.help: Removes the one-time code from SSH logins. The users' codes stay stored on the server.
remove.meaning: Afterwards the SSH key alone is enough again.
remove.heading: Remove SSH 2FA on {name}?

start.label: Start
start.help: Starts {tool}. The protection is back afterwards.

restart.label: Restart
restart.help: Restarts {tool}, for example after a configuration change. Protection is briefly missing.

stop.label: Stop
stop.help: Stops {tool}. Until it starts again the server bans no one.

disable.label: Autostart off
disable.help: {tool} no longer starts on its own after a server reboot.

allowlist.title: Allowlist (never ban)
allowlist.help: Rewrites the allowlist and reloads it. The address LCM uses to reach the server is always added.

uninstall.label: Uninstall
uninstall.heading: Remove {tool} from {name}?
uninstall.message: Package, service and configuration are deleted.

acl.title: ACL
acl.noFs: File system does not support ACLs

install.label: Install ACL support
install.help: Installs the “acl” package. Without ACLs the directory permissions of permission profiles have no effect on this server. The next scan checks whether they work.
install.heading: Install ACL support on {name}?

harden.title: Directory permissions
harden.subtitle: A permission profile grants rights, it takes none away. Here you remove world access.
harden.applyHelp: Removes world access. The group is set first so a service like nginx (www-data) keeps access. With a service, LCM checks afterwards that it still runs and reverts the change right away otherwise.

suggest.title: Standard directories
suggest.label: Find suggestions
suggest.help: Looks for data areas (/srv, /opt, /var/www, /data) and known configuration directories that are still readable by everyone, and suggests the group of the contents for each.
suggest.meaning: Read only, nothing changes on the server.
suggest.none: Nothing found, the known directories are already closed.

harden.heading: Lock down {count} directory(ies) on {name}?
harden.message: Afterwards only owner and group have access.
harden.restoreMessage: Permissions and group go back to the state before the lock-down.

error.meta: No special characters or wildcards such as ; | & $ * ? [ ] in the path.
error.unit: A service name without spaces, slashes and special characters.

cve.unusedHint: From Docker images no container uses. Shown but not counted: an image that runs nowhere offers no attack surface.
cve.listening: Weighted higher because they listen on ports reachable from outside:

notes.firewall_backend: Tool: {backend}. LCM checks during the run which one is installed; an existing one takes precedence.
notes.firewall_disable_open: The firewall then filters nothing, all ports are open again. The rules stay saved.
notes.firewall_install: If the tool is missing, LCM installs {backend} first.
notes.firewall_default_deny: Everything not allowed is then blocked. Ports {ports} stay open.
notes.ssh_port_unchanged: The server already uses port {port}, nothing changes.
notes.ssh_port_verify: LCM first tests port {port} with a new connection. If that fails, the old port stays.
notes.ssh_port_firewall: The firewall opens port {new} first and closes port {old} only after the switch.
notes.ssh_port_reconnect: SSH then runs on port {new}. You need to update clients and scripts using port {old}.
notes.root_login_locked: root can no longer log in directly via SSH.
notes.root_login_allowed: root can log in directly via SSH again. That is a popular target for attacks.
notes.root_login_lcm_unaffected: LCM logs in with its own user and is not affected.
notes.root_login_neutralize: If a preceding line in sshd_config keeps the lock from working, LCM disables that line.
notes.ssh_keys_only: Logging in then only works with a key, passwords are rejected.
notes.ssh_passwords_back: Logging in with a password works again, as far as the base configuration allows it.
notes.security_tool_allowlist: LCM's address ({ip}) goes on the allowlist so LCM does not lock itself out.
notes.allowlist_unresolved: The selected IP allowlists are empty or cannot be resolved and therefore protect nothing.
notes.crowdsec_bouncer: The firewall bouncer blocks detected attackers directly in the firewall.
notes.security_tool_installed_check: LCM first checks that {tool} is installed.
notes.security_tool_uninstall: Package, service and configuration of {tool} are removed. The server loses this protection.
notes.security_tool_unprotected: While {tool} is not running, it blocks no attackers.
notes.ssh_2fa_probe: LCM then checks with a new connection that it can still log in. If that fails, everything is rolled back.
notes.ssh_2fa_users: Each user then sets up their one-time password with google-authenticator.
notes.ssh_2fa_secrets_kept: The users' TOTP keys stay in place and work again right away when you set it up again.
notes.repos_update_rollback: If the package manager fails afterwards, LCM reverts the change.
notes.repos_unencrypted: These sources then run unencrypted again.
notes.repo_add: The signing key of {name} is downloaded and the source is added signed.
notes.apt_cache_probe: Package downloads then go through {url}. LCM tests this right away and undoes it on errors; if the cache cannot do HTTPS, HTTPS sources go direct.
notes.apt_cache_direct: The server then downloads packages directly from the sources again.
notes.apt_cache_enforced: A policy rule of the group connects the server again at the next health check.
notes.dns_unmanage: LCM stops managing DNS and restores the previous state.
notes.dns_test_rollback: LCM checks name resolution with {domain}; if it breaks, LCM reverts the change.
notes.timezone: Schedules (cron) and logs then show the local time of {timezone}. The clock itself stays correct.
notes.ntp_sync_check: The time service is restarted, and LCM waits until synchronisation is confirmed.

pins_written.one: 1 pin is written to the server: protection file against cleanup or a frozen version.
pins_written.other: {count} pins are written to the server: protection files against cleanup and frozen versions.

notes.path_harden: All other users lose access; before that the directory gets the service's group.
notes.path_harden_unit: LCM then checks that {unit} is still running.
notes.host_trivy: LCM then turns on the CVE scan by itself.
notes.host_apt_cacher: The cache is then reachable at {url} and is entered in the settings.
notes.host_crowdsec_lapi: The LAPI then listens on port {port}; LCM enters the credentials in the settings.
notes.docker_compose_recreate: The containers of {project} are recreated with the new images and are briefly unavailable.
notes.docker_pull_no_recreate: Running containers are not recreated; the new image takes effect at the next start.
notes.docker_prune_unused: Removes all images no container uses. Running containers are not affected.
notes.docker_cve_rescan: LCM then checks the images again for updates and CVEs.
notes.user_lock: {user} can no longer log in, not even with a key.
notes.user_remove_home: The account {user} is deleted together with its home directory.
